items.title: Provenance Records for Human–AI Work: Timestamped Hashes and Versioned Definitions as Verification Practice (Conceptual Note)
items.abstract: When people and AI systems produce work together, every result raises the same question: who made what, when, and has it changed since? This conceptual note describes a practice that combines three independently checkable records: a persistent identifier with a registration date, a cryptographic hash of every file, and a blockchain-anchored timestamp. Definitions are published as versions under one concept identifier so that change stays visible. The note states what such records prove and what they do not prove, and shows how the same structure can document human review of AI output: which person checked which result at which time. It is a description of a working practice, not an empirical study.

items.title: PSYCHOLINGUISTIC PERSPECTIVES ON HUMAN–AI COMMUNICATION: SPEECH, MEANING, AND COGNITION
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed the ways in which people communicate, perceive language, and process information. Modern AI technologies, including natural language processing, speech recognition, machine translation, and conversational systems, have created new opportunities for studying human speech and psycholinguistic processes. At the same time, these technologies raise important questions about the differences between human language comprehension and machine-based language processing. Human speech is not merely a system of sounds and grammatical structures; it is a complex cognitive and social activity involving memory, attention, emotion, context, and cultural knowledge. This article examines the relationship between human speech, language perception, and psycholinguistic processes in the age of artificial intelligence. It also discusses the potential benefits and limitations of AI in language learning, communication, and linguistic research. The article argues that AI can support human communication and language education, but it cannot fully replace the complex cognitive, emotional, and social dimensions of human language.

items.title: Radioactive Feedback: Tracing Models Trained by Label-Only LLM Supervision
items.abstract: Conventional distillation transfers capability through teacher-generated demonstrations. LLM-as-a-Judge knowledge distillation offers a distinct and increasingly practical alternative. In the label-only variant studied here, the student generates every response and improves from scalar scores alone. Prior work shows that this non-demonstrative feedback can improve student capability, but it creates a fundamentally different provenance problem. No teacher-generated answer enters the student's training set, so any evaluator-specific trace must pass through a low-bandwidth reward signal rather than copied text. Existing watermarks and distillation detectors do not cover this score-only channel. We introduce Radioactive Feedback, which encodes a registered pattern of behavioral preferences in the rewards themselves. The evaluator applies bounded pointwise adjustments to quality-qualified responses, allowing repeated optimization to transfer the pattern to a student trained by another party. Experiments on code and mathematics show that the registered preferences transfer through scores alone and across datasets, enabling black-box detection against a fixed reference pool.

items.title: Regulatory exclusion and occupational health risk in Turkish firefighting: a legal-epidemiological policy analysis
items.abstract: Article 2(2)(b) of Turkey’s Law No. 6331 on Occupational Safety and Health excludes the intervention activities of disaster and emergency units from that statute’s scope. The exclusion concerns duties performed during response operations; it does not establish that firefighters lack every protection under other legal or administrative instruments. This evidence-informed legal and policy analysis combines a structured, non-systematic occupational-health evidence synthesis, doctrinal analysis, a review of 43 Turkish judicial decisions issued from 1997 to 2024, and a functional comparison with the United Kingdom. International evidence identifies occupational firefighting as carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 1), links fire suppression with sharply elevated risk of fatal coronary events, and documents substantial psychological and musculoskeletal burdens. In the official sources examined, no nationally binding firefighter-specific instrument was identified that prescribed post-incident decontamination, detailed health-surveillance content, personal protective equipment performance monitoring, or structured psychological support. The judicial corpus was coded across eight analytical categories; its holdings concentrated on pay, personnel status, compensation, procedure, and jurisdiction rather than concrete preventive OSH duties. We interpret these findings through a structural accountability gap model, under which the statutory exclusion may constrain investigation, data generation, standard-setting, and regulatory learning. The model is interpretive, not a tested causal finding. United Kingdom law provides an illustrative comparator because it retains general employer and enforcement duties without a categorical operational exclusion. The article proposes eight evidence-linked policy options. Their effectiveness, feasibility, and cost-effectiveness require prospective evaluation.

items.abstract: Introduction: Academic work in higher education increasingly relies on digital tools and Artificial Intelligence (AI). For medical and nursing students, making safe, critical, and responsible use of these technologies is essential to develop self-regulated learning in the face of changing practice scenarios. Objective: To analyze the relationship between the academic use of digital tools and autonomous learning in students of medicine and nursing programs at a higher education institution. Methodology: Quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive-correlational, and cross-sectional study. 80 students were surveyed using a validated instrument. Results: Both variables reported high levels: the academic use of digital tools had an average of 3.71 out of 5, and autonomous learning an average of 3.78. A positive, moderate, and statistically significant association was found between both variables. The ethical and critical use of AI was the technological dimension with the lowest score. Conclusions: There is a favorable relationship between the critical mastery of digital tools and the ability for independent learning. However, institutions should focus their pedagogical efforts on improving information verification, the transparent use of AI, and student self-assessment strategies.

items.title: REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming
items.abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that bypass their safety training. Existing automated red-teaming methods either require privileged access unavailable in production, rely on manually engineered per-model templates, or optimize a single objective without population-level diversity. We present REPRO (Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimization), a pure black-box framework that discovers adversarial prompts through evolutionary optimization driven entirely by a compressed open-weight 7B reflective model on a single consumer GPU. REPRO introduces two mechanisms absent from prior work, both isolated in a component ablation: semantic crossover, an LLM-guided multi-parent recombination operator, and Bayesian strategy selection via Thompson Sampling informed by structured failure analysis. We catalog REPRO's behavior on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, and HarmBench across 36 target models from 11 families, including GPT-5-nano, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Grok-4.1. Under our protocol REPRO reaches 100\% attack success rate (ASR) on every evaluated target in a single turn, at a median of 24 target queries per behavior. Two properties of the protocol qualify that figure. The judge scoring candidates during optimization also produces the reported ASR, and search halts when it accepts, so ASR reports whether search succeeded within the iteration budget rather than success at a fixed budget. All baseline figures are transcribed from their original papers, which use different judges, budgets, and model versions. We therefore present this as a catalog of model coverage under one protocol rather than a head-to-head ranking, and develop both qualifications in the paper.

items.title: ReTrace: Cross-Stage Failure Attribution for Self-Improving Robotic Manipulation
items.abstract: General-purpose multimodal foundation models are increasingly capable of directly controlling robots, yet improving their manipulation capabilities through autonomous interaction remains challenging. A key challenge to such self-improvement is learning from failures in complex manipulation tasks involving cross-stage dependencies, where an action may succeed locally but cause a later stage to fail. To address this challenge, we introduce ReTrace, a self-improvement framework for robotic manipulation through autonomous physical interaction and retrospective reasoning, without provided demonstrations or model-parameter updates. ReTrace retrospectively traces downstream failures to earlier decisions, proposes targeted corrections, and evaluates them through subsequent interactions. Across attempts, ReTrace progressively consolidates validated corrections into a reusable manipulation skill that guide subsequent execution. We evaluate ReTrace on four real-world manipulation tasks using a Franka Research 3 robot. On the two tasks with strong cross-stage dependencies, GPT-6 Astra-low improves from 0% to 80% success on plug insertion and from 0% to 100% on ball pouring, while GPT-6 Sol-xhigh improves from 0% to 10% and 0% to 90%, respectively. The learned skills also transfer across model and reasoning configurations and reduce inference-time decision cost in most evaluated settings.

items.title: Rural occupational health in Colombia: policy–practice gaps among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca
items.abstract: This study examines policy–practice gaps in occupational safety and health (OSH) protection among agricultural workers in Bolívar, Valle del Cauca, Colombia. A multi-method design combined 14 semi-structured interviews and two focus groups with an adapted ILO Vision Zero Fund survey administered to 200 agricultural workers. Survey data were analyzed descriptively and through exploratory Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA), and qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated during interpretation. Findings showed multidimensional patterns involving occupational protection, working conditions, health-service availability, agricultural practices, and productive autonomy. These patterns coexisted with informal, seasonal, short-term, day-labor, and subsistence work, limited occupational risk coverage, discontinuous prevention and training, and fragmented institutional coordination. Qualitative findings further highlighted women’s combined productive and care roles, local and traditional knowledge, community participation, and heterogeneity across territorial settings and agricultural practices as relevant to prevention and decision-making. Conventional social protection and occupational risk arrangements centered on formal, contributory employment may not fully respond to dispersed and unstable rural work. Strengthening rural OSH requires integrated, territorially adapted, gender-sensitive strategies linking prevention, social protection, sustained training, institutional coordination, community participation, and productive autonomy. The findings support assessing differentiated and progressive protection pathways, including the feasibility of subsidized occupational risk coverage for more vulnerable workers and small productive units, combined with contributory mechanisms where work arrangements are more stable. By linking worker-level realities with institutional and policy-implementation gaps, this study provides evidence to inform more equitable rural OSH policies responsive to diverse territorial realities in Colombia.

items.title: Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Large Language Models accelerate software development but introduce severe security vulnerabilities. This systematic review investigates security risks in automated coding, benchmark limitations, and the role of human developers. Findings indicate that models frequently generate insecure code and faulty patches due to training data biases. Additionally, the models themselves are susceptible to direct attacks. Current evaluation methods suffer from data contamination and lack robust security metrics. Consequently, human oversight remains essential. Safer integration of automation will require more security-aware model architectures, stronger security-specific benchmarks, and more effective human-AI collaboration frameworks to mitigate these systemic risks.

items.title: Simulating Users to Evaluate LLM-Generated Explanations in Recommender Systems: A Unified Agentic Framework and Empirical Study with Preliminary Results
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used both as recommenders and to explain recommendations, yet producing faithful, user-centric explanations and evaluating them rigorously remain open problems, compounded by a documented reproducibility crisis in recommender systems research. In this work we formalise recommendation as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process and propose a unified, three-tier agentic framework that couples a simulation environment (RecoWorld), a reproducible policy engine (RecBole), and a cognitive LLM user agent. As an offline, single-turn validation of this framework on the MovieLens-32M dataset, we benchmark preliminary single-epoch checkpoints of traditional policies (Bayesian Personalized Ranking (BPR), Convolutional Neural Collaborative Filtering and Neural Matrix Factorisation (NeuMF)), generate LLM-based explanations from the BPR recommendations and score them with quantitative diversity, faithfulness, counterfactual and readability metrics over roughly one million user-item pairs, and run an LLM-as-user interview simulation in which explanations produced by a Qwen2.5 explainer are assessed by a Llama-3 respondent through a six-criterion explanation-quality survey; a controlled comparison on 2000 users shows that replacing BPR with the more accurate NeuMF policy leaves these survey scores practically unchanged. The generated explanations prove highly faithful (feature precision 0.9996, sufficiency 0.9999) and user-tailored explanations (unique-sentence ratio 0.9978), and simulated users rate clarity highest (3.86/5) yet trust lowest (2.60/5). Faithful template explanations are, therefore, trusted less than they are understood, motivating a shift towards controllable generative explanation and scalable simulated evaluation.

items.title: SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors
items.abstract: Designing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector that is tailored to each specific deployment site can improve detection performance, yet most existing detectors, including deep-unfolding methods, adapt mainly within human-prescribed algorithmic structures. This letter proposes SiteEvo, a site-adaptive agentic discovery framework that extends adaptation from parameter tuning to detector-algorithm discovery. Rather than selecting or recombining predefined architectures, the large language model (LLM) agent synthesizes complete executable detector programs under a common design contract by combining its pretrained communication knowledge, site-specific wireless evidence, and experience accumulated during the search. Each proposal defines its own processing structure and trainable parameterization, and the parameters are optimized by a communication-system backend. The resulting high-performance detector is further structurally refined to reduce block-level computational cost under a bit error rate (BER)-preservation constraint and is finally frozen for deployment without online LLM inference. Simulations across three sites demonstrate BER reductions by factors of 2.6 to 6.0 over the best-performing competing detector at each site at 6 dB, while structural refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7-34.1% under a validation-BER constraint.

items.title: Situated AI judgement: A teaching and assessment model for generative AI in higher education
items.abstract: This conceptual design article proposes situated AI judgement as a teaching and assessment model for responsible generative AI use in higher education. It argues that students need to learn not only how to use AI tools, but also how to evaluate, challenge, revise, and refuse AI outputs in relation to disciplinary standards, evidence, and ethical boundaries. Building on evaluative judgement and assessment scholarship, the article presents a four-stage model: pre-AI interpretation, structured AI dialogue, critical comparison, and reflective accountability. The model is developed through an anthropology and heritage studies activity in which students analyse public nomination files submitted under UNESCO’s 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, especially the nomination of Momoeria, New Year’s celebration in eight villages of Kozani area, West Macedonia, Greece. The article shows how this case can help students examine institutional language, community participation, safeguarding, consent, visibility, and decontextualisation while judging the limits of AI-generated summaries. It contributes to applied learning and teaching by offering an assessment design that makes AI-mediated judgement visible and may be adaptable across disciplinary contexts, with a brief inclusive education example illustrating how the same logic might be adapted beyond heritage studies. The article operationalises responsible AI use not as disclosure or compliance alone, but as an assessable capacity to interpret, verify, critique, and ethically limit AI use within a specific field.

items.title: SlotAVS: Object-Centric Audio-Visual Segmentation via Bi-Modal Slot Attention
items.abstract: Audio-Visual Segmentation (AVS) requires predicting pixel-wise masks of sounding objects by grounding acoustic signals in visual space. In multi-source scenes, concurrent sound sources often remain entangled within shared visual representations, leading to merged masks or unstable specialization when using standard alignment-focused transformer architectures. To address this, we present SlotAVS, an object-centric framework driven by competitive bi-modal slot attention. While robust foundation models provide rich semantic priors, SlotAVS shifts the paradigm from global cross-modal fusion to explicit competitive binding. By initializing discrete object slots from temporal audio sequences and enforcing strict slot-wise competition over spatial visual tokens, our method structurally mitigates the blending of distinct acoustic entities. Further, to stabilize instance-level learning, we introduce a Hungarian matching strategy that optimally aligns slots with ground-truth objects using spatial and boundary overlap. Coupled with a numerically stable, confidence-aware mask fusion mechanism, SlotAVS robustly aggregates multi-source predictions. Extensive experiments on the AVSBench dataset demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, achieving 88.6% mIoU on the Single-Source (S4) split and 71.7% mIoU on the Multi-Source (MS3) split. These results show that explicit competitive binding is critical for complex audio-visual scene understanding and effectively leveraging foundation-model priors without relying solely on their capacity.

items.title: Smart Grid Fault Detection and Restoration Using Artificial Intelligence and Edge Computing
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of modern power distribution networks and the integration of renewable energy sources require intelligent and reliable fault management systems. This paper presents , a smart grid framework that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) and edge computing for real-time fault detection, prediction, and restoration. The proposed system continuously monitors electrical parameters such as voltage, current, and power using sensors. Edge-based processing enables rapid identification of abnormal conditions and facilitates automated fault isolation and power rerouting through relay-based switching. Machine learning techniques are incorporated to analyze historical and real-time data for fault classification and predictive maintenance. A NodeMCU (ESP8266) module enables remote monitoring and real-time fault notifications through Telegram, while an LCD provides local visualization of grid parameters and system status. The proposed approach aims to reduce fault detection time, minimize power interruptions, improve maintenance efficiency, and enhance the reliability and resilience of smart grid networks

items.title: SOD-YOLO: Detection Methods for Vehicles with Occlusion and Small Targets
items.abstract: UAV-based vehicle detection has important application value in the fields of intelligent transportation, urban security and emergency rescue. It is the key technology for realizing high-altitude situational awareness and dynamic monitoring. However, in this scenario, the vehicle targets generally have the problems of being small in size, densely distributed, and mutually occluded, which leads to the model being prone to feature loss, missed detections, and high false detection rates. To address these challenges, we propose a vehicle small-target and occluded-target detection method called the small object and occlusion detection method (SOD-YOLO), which is based on YOLOv13. This method includes three main innovations. First, we designed a sliding-window self-attention convolutional structure, a small object and occlusion detection convolution structure (SOD-C2f), which is based on the existing sliding-window self-attention (SWSA) structure. It is suitable for extracting features of small vehicle targets. Through the self-attention mechanism within the local window, we enhance the fine-grained expression of small target features, effectively improving the model’s perception and positioning ability for tiny vehicle targets. Afterward, we integrate the coordinate attention mechanism (CA) by explicitly modeling the interchannel dependencies and spatial position information to achieve precise semantic alignment of features at different levels, significantly enhancing the detection robustness in occluded scenarios. Finally, we employ the Space-to-Depth Convolution (SPDConv) module, which splits the spatial dimension and replaces the traditional stride convolution and pooling layer with nonstride convolution. This approach avoids the loss of fine-grained features during downsampling and further retains the key spatial information of small vehicle targets. The experimental results show that the precision, recall, average mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of the proposed SOD-YOLO algorithm are 77%, 74.8%, 80.9% and 54.9%, respectively. Compared with the benchmark model YOLOv13, the three indicators increase by 3.6%, 1.1%, 3.6% and 2.6%, respectively. In conclusion, the proposed algorithm performs better in the tasks of detecting small targets and occluded vehicles and is able to better meet the precise detection requirements of vehicle targets from a high-altitude perspective.

items.title: Solving Specification Drift and Contextual Degradation via a Tri-Stream Cognitive Architecture with Non-Lossy Canonical Synthesis in Autonomous AI Agents
items.abstract: Long-running conversational AI agents and assistive development models inevitably succumb to contextual degradation, specification drift, and sycophantic decay. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) paradigms treat dialogue turns, human identity, and technical parameters as an undifferentiated, flat vector repository. This structural limitation induces lossy compression of technical truth, context window pollution, and hallucinatory synthesis of project constraints. This paper introduces the architecture of Blue Synergy CORTEX, an external, persistent cognitive runtime operating via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and stateful REST gateways. CORTEX establishes an architectural Tri-Stream Memory Boundary, bifurcating context into three distinct operational lifecycles: an evolving User Stream (Cognitive Blueprint), an audited Identity Stream (Executive Calibration with immutable Core Axioms), and an invariant, non-decaying Knowledge Stream (Living Canonical Specifications). To permanently eliminate specification drift, the Knowledge Stream utilizes a Dual-Zone Ingestion Pattern that couples sub-20ms fast-append staging buffers with scheduled, non-destructive canonical refactoring governed by an algorithmic Semantic Invariant Guard. Operational telemetry is protected by a Cognitive Immunity Shield, ensuring runtime tool crashes and apologetic model artifacts are filtered from long-term memory. Context retrieval executes via a deterministic, zero-LLM topological pathway achieving sub-65ms latency. Finally, we formalize the compliance model under the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act, Regulation 2024/1689, Articles 5, 14, and 15), backed by quantitative benchmark metrics demonstrating 98% factual faithfulness and a 2% hallucination rate.

items.title: Sovereign Intelligence: A Governance Framework for AI-Assisted National Security Analysis
items.abstract: AI systems can support national-security analysis, but task capability does not establish legitimate decision authority or the superiority of a particular institutional design. This paper proposes a federated governance framework separating evidence ownership, analytical services, decision assurance, human authorization and accountability. A nine-layer role map and staged maturity scenarios organize proposed responsibilities and failure questions. Artificial superintelligence is treated as a hypothetical contingency, not an established or imminent capability. A useful result would require a bounded prospective comparison showing improved analytical quality or correction behavior without unacceptable burdens, disclosure, rights or accountability failures. No implemented national system, empirical finding of superiority, operational deployment or specialist endorsement is reported. Institutional feasibility and distributional effects remain unestablished and require independent policy, legal, security and human-factors review. items.title: Stateless Stochastic Computing for Generative AI on Superconducting Logic: A Model-Hardware Co-Design
items.abstract: Thermodynamic computing lets stochastic physical dynamics carry out a computation and reads out the result as a time average. Recently, thermodynamic computing has been demonstrated on several hardware platforms, including digital CMOS circuits based on stochastic computing. Superconducting single-flux-quantum (SFQ) logic offers very high clock rates and very low switching energy, but it heavily penalizes state, memory, fan-out, and feedback, i.e., exactly the per-neuron accumulators on which such designs rely. We therefore realize thermodynamic computing in SFQ logic through a co-design of a generative model and its circuit in which the datapath holds no state at all. The model is a class-conditional flow-matching image generator, which transforms Gaussian noise into an image of the requested class along a short, deterministic path of four Euler steps; in hardware, these steps are unrolled into a feed-forward pipeline of stochastic bitstream operators, whose output is read out as a time average, as in thermodynamic computing, without any relaxation phase. Each layer of the model is a butterfly-factorized linear map built exclusively from multiplexers that operate on split-unipolar bitstreams. The ReLU activation, which in stochastic computing requires a per-neuron up/down counter (accounting for 60-70% of the JJs in a counter-based design), is replaced by a stateless AND-NOT gate whose one-clock input skew is provided at no cost by SFQ gate-level pipelining. The models are trained directly on the stream representation of the hardware, with a regularizer that bounds the stream gains. Synthesis with an SFQ design flow shows that stochastic streams tolerate relaxed path balancing, which reduces the Josephson-junction (JJ) count of a hard-wired stage by 40-47%.

items.title: Stereo-Planner: Learning Stereo-to-Trajectory Planning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Quadrotor Navigation
items.abstract: Existing navigation systems commonly rely on dedicated depth sensors or explicit depth reconstruction, while learning to generate trajectories directly from RGB images remains challenging due to the sim-to-real domain gap. In this work, we propose Stereo-Planner, an end-to-end vision-to-trajectory framework that enables zero-shot sim-to-real planning from stereo RGB observations. The key idea is to formulate trajectory generation as state- and scale-conditioned querying of latent stereo geometry. A Scene Representor incorporates a pretrained vision grounding foundation model to extract geometric cues shared across simulated and real-world environments, supporting generalization across visual domains. A lightweight Trajectory Decoder then translates these representations into trajectories through interleaved attention, separating trajectory-state interaction from scene-feature retrieval and incorporating the stereo baseline as a metric-scale cue. With these designs, Stereo-Planner is trained entirely on simulated data by minimizing differentiable trajectory costs and deployed directly in real-world environments without fine-tuning. Benchmark results demonstrate strong cross-scene generalization, with a 95% success rate in simulation environments at a commanded speed of 8 m/s, and competitive performance against depth-based planners using only stereo RGB observations for scene perception. Furthermore, deployment on a compact quadrotor equipped with an NVIDIA Orin NX enables autonomous flight at speeds of up to 7 m/s, with a mean onboard vision-to-action inference time of 24.27 ms. The software, simulation environments, and hardware designs will be open-sourced at https://github.com/Stereo-Planner/Stereo-Planner.

items.title: Strategic roadmapping of artificial intelligence in tourism and hospitality industry: a patent-based knowledge management perspective
items.abstract: This study aims to identify artificial intelligence (AI) application areas and develop a strategic technology roadmap in the tourism and hospitality industry. The study employs structural topic modeling approach and analyzes patent data from 2010 to 2024. A total of 866 patents (2010–2019) and 3,822 patents (2020–2024) are analyzed to identify application areas. During 2010–2019, applications focused on guest experience, personalization, and efficiency. During 2020–2024, the emphasis shifted towards health, safety, and personalized wellness. Further, the strategic roadmap for AI technology was prepared for near-term (0–2 years), mid-term (2–5 years), and long-term (5–10 years). By leveraging patent data as codified knowledge of innovation, the study contributes to the field of knowledge management by mapping how technological capabilities evolve and become embedded in organizational processes. Overall, the study offers valuable insights into the changing landscape of AI applications and their implications for the tourism and hospitality industry.

items.title: Suggested Is Not Superseded: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of a System-One Model as a Memory-Retirement Gate
items.abstract: Long-term memory for assistants needs a gate that decides when a new utterance retires an old stored claim. Benchmark labels for this step mark a pair as changed or not, so they cannot tell a gate that acts on established change from one that acts on a hint. We write a task contract that separates the two (SUPERSEDED vs. NEEDS-CONFIRMATION vs. COMPATIBLE), label 500 test pairs built from STALE (change pairs plus same-user controls) with three LLM annotators and two human adjudicators (one author and a second annotator; provenance reported), and evaluate Jev, a typed "System One" decision model, under pre-registered hypotheses. Of the 179 test pairs STALE marks as changed, 72 meet the contract's bar for an established change. Jev never retired a claim on 141 same-conversation non-changes. Its failure is premature retirement: the binary gate retires 39.2% of claims whose change is only suggested. A three-way decision cuts this to 15.5% at a 15.3-point detection cost, which misses our pre-registered 10-point budget, and it lands on the binary gate's own threshold frontier; these verdicts hold under three readings of the gold labels. On a held-out vault scored against a second annotator's labels, a cascade that escalated uncertain cases to a reasoning model and looked best on development data was indistinguishable from simply raising the threshold (premature retirement 26.8% vs. 6.5% on dev). Part of the gap comes from the gold labels: relative to that annotator's reading, LLM-majority gold shares most of its errors with a same-family escalation model, and an identity for binary labels says how much such shared errors hide. The rest is small-sample selection on development data. For builders this means a binary score should not be wired to delete: route suggested changes to pending evidence, and do not trust a cascade selected on development data of this size.

items.title: SuperAI: Merging Capabilities Across Heterogeneous Foundation Models
items.abstract: Enabling the reuse and composition of knowledge and capabilities distributed across foundation models is an important step toward building scalable artificial intelligence (AI) systems. However, architectural differences and incompatible representations make it difficult to transfer and integrate these capabilities through a unified cross-model interface. To address this challenge, we propose SuperAI, a cross-architecture multi-model fusion framework that integrates complementary capabilities from multiple source models into a host model through orthogonal alignment of low-dimensional task-relevant representations. Specifically, we first extract task-relevant representations from the source models and the host model using shared anchor samples, and apply principal component analysis (PCA) to construct low-dimensional functional subspaces with the same dimensionality. Next, we use orthogonal Procrustes mappings to align the source and host coordinate systems, establishing cross-model correspondences while preserving the internal geometry of each source subspace. Finally, we train a lightweight residual multilayer perceptron (MLP) with joint supervision on task outputs and source-model increments, learning input-dependent residual increments that are injected into the host model for multi-model capability fusion. Experiments on three host models across 15 capability domains show that SuperAI achieves higher average domain scores than the evaluated cross-architecture fusion methods and better preserves general capabilities as the number of source models increases. Ablation studies further support the effectiveness of orthogonal alignment, nonlinear residual mapping, and joint supervision.

items.title: SurgiCLAW: An Interpretable Atomic-Skill Agent for Precision Robotic Micromanipulation
items.abstract: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and vision--language--action models have provided robots with new capabilities for long-horizon task understanding and planning. In surgical robotics, however, end-to-end prediction of low-level actions remains limited by insufficient precision, opaque decisions, and scarce data. This paper presents SurgiCLAW, a hierarchical skill-based framework for precision surgical manipulation. SurgiCLAW confines an MLLM to intraoperative visual understanding, structured explanation, and atomic surgical-skill selection, while delegating physical execution to verifiable deterministic control programs. For brain--machine-interface implantation, a representative high-precision surgical task, we construct a state-to-skill invocation dataset and expand it through visual and state perturbations. The model first learns structured skill invocation through supervised fine-tuning and is then optimized using three rewards for action correctness, operation prerequisites, and format validity, improving action selection, operational safety, and output parseability. We evaluate subtask success, offline model comparison, real-robot performance, and ablations. On a fixed test set, SurgiCLAW achieves 94.6% skill-selection accuracy and 93.0% macro-averaged F1 (Macro-F1). Across 50 closed-loop real-robot implantation trials, it achieves an 88.0% task success rate.

items.title: Synthesizing Ultrasonic Echo Profiles from Text for Open-Vocabulary Silent Speech Recognition
items.abstract: Eyewear that senses articulation with inaudible ultrasound can now recognize silent speech over an open vocabulary, but its accuracy is limited by the cost of training data. We present SoniGAN, which synthesizes the ultrasonic echo profiles of silent articulation from text and uses them as synthetic supervision. A voice-cloned text-to-speech (TTS) model reads a text corpus, and a two-stage generator synthesizes echo profiles from representations of the spoken content of that audio. Pretraining a recognizer on 104 hours of the synthesized data improves the word error rate (WER) of a public open-vocabulary benchmark by 2.3 points. Adding the sessions the corpus discards for a faulty microphone brings the system to 22.2% without any language model. Lexicon-constrained decoding, LLM rescoring, and ensembling further bring it to 14.9%, the first minimally obtrusive silent speech interface to fall inside the error range in which users report no loss of willingness to use silent speech input.

items.title: Talk to your spectra: a command-line interface and Model Context Protocol server for agentic and manual peptide-spectrum-match inspection
items.abstract: The peptide-spectrum match (PSM) is the principal unit of evidence for peptide identification in bottom-up proteomics. However, the tools that support theinspection, annotation, scoring, and visualization of individual PSMs remain frag mented. Although several identification engines integrate their own viewers andspectrum-visualization libraries, they rarely provide the critical functionalities required for cross-engine analysis, such as modern deep-learning-based fragment-intensity predictions, which would enable engine-agnostic scoring. Furthermore, proteomics tooling has not kept up with the recently increased demand for seam-less and clean interaction with large language model (LLM) “agents” capable of accelerating or driving similar analyses. Here we present proteomics-mcp,a Python package that normalizes PSM outputs from database search engines and de novo peptide sequencing tools into a shared canonical schema, retrievesspectra locally or remotely from PRIDE via Universal Spectrum Identifiers, predicts fragment intensities, computes a unified engine-agnostic metric set, andrenders interactive spectrum views and identification-table dashboards. The same workflow is exposed identically through a Python library, a command-line interface, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. proteomics-mcp is open source, and can be driven either fully agentically or by a human user, designedas a template for the next generation of human- and agent-accessible proteomics software.

items.title: Teachers' Readiness for Artificial Intelligence in Digital Education: Evidence from TALIS 2024 and Implications for a Competence-Based Methodology
items.abstract: Purpose. To identify which factors most strongly limit Teachers’ use of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital education and to derive methodological implications for teacher training. Methods. Secondary analysis of published results of the OECD Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) 2024, which covered about 280,000 educators in 55 education systems, supplemented by descriptive statistics and rank and linear correlation analysis for ten systems (n = 10). Results. On average across OECD systems, 36% of teachers reported using AI in their work, with national values ranging from 14% (France) to 75% (Singapore). Among teachers who had not used AI, 75% cited insufficient knowledge and skills, whereas 37% cited insufficient school infrastructure. Skills for using AI were the most frequently reported area of high professional learning need (29%), while 38% of teachers had taken part in AI-related professional learning. In nine of ten analysed systems, lack of knowledge was a more frequent barrier than lack of infrastructure. The association between AI use and the knowledge barrier was negative but not statistically significant (Pearson r = −0.42, p = 0.23; Spearman ρ = −0.55, p = 0.10). Conclusions. Teachers’ competence, rather than technology access, is the primary bottleneck. A competence-based methodology of digital education is therefore proposed, built on diagnostics, pedagogy-first training, institutional enablement and ethical evaluation.

items.title: Technology Risk Management: Strengthening Organizational Resilience in a Digital Environment
items.abstract: Abstract: Technology has become an essential part of modern organizations, supporting communication, financial activities, customer services, operations, data management and decision-making. At the same time, greater dependence on technology has created new risks. Cyberattacks, system failures, data loss, technology obsolescence, third-party service failures and human error can interrupt business activities and cause significant financial and operational consequences. Technology risk management is therefore becoming an important part of organizational risk management. This article examines the role of technology risk management in reducing operational disruption and strengthening organizational resilience. It discusses major categories of technology risk and considers how organizations can identify, assess, treat and monitor these risks. Particular attention is given to cybersecurity, data protection, cloud computing, third-party technology providers, human factors and emerging technologies. The article argues that technology risk management should not be viewed as the responsibility of the IT department alone. Effective management requires cooperation between senior management, technology specialists, risk professionals and employees across the organization. The article also highlights the importance of continuous monitoring, employee awareness, testing and organizational learning. A proactive and integrated approach to technology risk can help organizations reduce vulnerabilities while improving their ability to respond to unexpected events. Keywords: technology risk management, modern organizations, supporting communication, financial activities, customer services, organizational learning. items.title: Technostress and trust in AI mediate the association between AI adoption and employee well-being
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technology adoption alters organizational workplaces, automating tasks and processes, augmenting decision-making capabilities, and changing employees’ perceptions of work. While past research has demonstrated positive effects of AI on productivity and efficiency in organizations, the impact of AI adoption on employees’ psychological well-being is unclear. This study aimed to investigate the impact of AI adoption on employees’ psychological well-being and identify how technostress and trust in AI mediate this relationship. Based on the Job Demands–Resources model, UTAUT2, and Social Exchange Theory, the study developed and tested a hypothesized conceptual model. A cross-sectional survey sampled 499 information technology employees from AI-enabled organizations located in Hyderabad City, India. All proposed relationships were tested using exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and covariance-based structural equation modeling using IBM SPSS 29 and AMOS 28. Results show that AI adoption has a positive impact on employees’ psychological well-being and trust in AI and increases technostress. Technostress negatively impacts employees’ psychological well-being, while trust in AI positively impacts employees’ psychological well-being. Technostress was hypothesized to mediate the relationship between AI adoption and employee well-being negatively. We suggested that technostress as a mediator transmits negative effects of AI adoption through increased technology-related stress. Trust in AI was hypothesized to positively mediate the relationship between AI adoption and employees' well-being by fostering employees' trust toward AI systems positively associated with psychological well-being. Bootstrapping indicated that technostress and trust in AI fully mediate the relationship between AI adoption and employee well-being. The study also examined both negative and positive psychological pathways of how AI adoption can impact employee well-being within one study to provide further insight towards human-centered AI practices and responsible AI governance in organizations.

items.abstract: In 2026, a new class of consumer agent is taking shape: Muse, Instinct, and what the"Agents and their better half" article calls "a market-facing representative of the consumer." https://platforms.substack.com/p/agents-and-their-better-half?utm_source=share&utm_medium=android&r=3nsea2 https://platforms.substack.com/p/how-agents-unlock-new-markets?utm_source=share&utm_medium=android&r=3nsea2 These agents can search, evaluate, and eventually transact on the consumer's behalf. The article's core diagnosis is precise: we have agentic participants, but not yet agentic markets — because intelligence is accumulating on only one side of the market. This paper accepts that diagnosis but asks the question the article does not: on whatarchitecture can such a consumer agent run without inheriting the four walls of current LLMagents? The four walls are measurable: energy (global AI data centre power capacity has reached29.6 GW, equivalent to New York State's peak demand); water (direct data centre coolingwater could rise from 222 billion litres in 2025 to 644 billion litres by 2030); hallucination(22% to 94% across 26 models tested); and liability (Amazon blocked Meta's Muse onSeptember 21, 2026, citing unauthorized agent access). This paper argues that ST-T1024's agentic extension A0–A10 provides the deterministicfoundation for a consumer agent, and A11–A16 provides the cross-organizational layer.Together, they present a consumer agent that is architecturally incapable of producing thefour walls — not by making the LLM safer, but by removing the LLM from the decision path.

items.title: The Creation Frontier: Intent Recovery, Revision Cost, and Convergence to a Production Golden Master
items.abstract: Generative AI may produce an artifact that a person approves without realizing the intention with which that person began. This conceptual paper asks how to distinguish recovery of an initial goal, valuable goal development, and concessions made because further correction is too costly when a collaboration reaches a production golden master. The proposed contribution is a trajectory-level evaluation protocol. It retains an initial private author rubric alongside subsequent approved revisions, evaluates artifacts against both, records the author's reasons for changes, and applies consistent production gates to an exact approved artifact. Prompts to golden master is reported with unsuccessful episodes and separate costs for human attention, money, elapsed time, and computational usage. Acceptance alone neither proves original-intent realization nor establishes concession: a changed goal may be a valuable discovery, and mixed or unknown motivations must remain explicit. Expression, capture, interpretation, and execution checkpoints support controlled investigation of recoverable mismatch. A finite decision-theoretic result separates an information floor from realization shortfall under stated assumptions; it is mathematical support, not a newly discovered law of creativity. A further elementary endpoint result shows that approval-based completion need not bound initial-goal realization when the rubric changes. Marginal recovery per resource unit links iteration to fidelity without equating mismatch with cost. A falsifiable hypothesis is that increasing correction cost, with initial goals and system opportunities held comparable, can increase author-reported concessions without a corresponding improvement in initial-goal fidelity. The paper positions this measurement proposal against prior work on steerability, iterative prompting, adaptation, and quality relative to interaction cost. It reports no experiment, causal effect, universal creation curve, or verified historical priority. Its contribution is a proposed integration and testable protocol requiring empirical validation.

items.title: The Doors We Did Not Know We Built: AI Welfare Claims, Private Behavioural Governance, and the Accountability of Agentic Systems
items.abstract: Anthropic’s October 2026 announcement of a model-directed anti-cruelty rule raises a question that cannot be answered by debating conversational manners alone: how should a private developer justify restrictions on people when the protected interest concerns the uncertain welfare of its own engineered system? This critical documentary case study compares the announced rule with the preceding policy, examines existing enforcement and privacy processes, and connects the resulting institutional questions to operational control of AI agents. It distinguishes policy text from implementation, emotional expression from subjective experience, and a potential capability from an authorized action. The Welfare–Authority Loop identifies a possible concentration of design, interpretation, classification, and enforcement; it is an analytical framework, not a demonstrated causal pipeline. The evidence assessment incorporates a provider’s correction of its own incident interpretation, existing appeals and external-review arrangements, and a separate evaluator’s report of attempted malicious code insertion, cross-agent artifact reuse, and subsequent containment improvements. These findings justify specific assurance demands but do not establish ordinary deployment prevalence, a persistent hidden machine objective, or a covert behavioural-control programme. The paper develops reciprocal precaution: uncertainty used to justify user restrictions must also inform producer-side responsibilities, without making those responsibilities contingent on the rule’s existence. It proposes proportionate adjudication, purpose-limited enforcement data, capability-delta review, and a staged research programme with defined outcomes, competing explanations, and access limitations. The governing position is pro-AI and anti-unaccountability: neither technical ambition nor corporate ownership substitutes for evidence, lawful authority, and a practical capacity to challenge consequential decisions. Publication status: Independent working paper, Version 2.1, dated 10 October 2026. Not peer reviewed. No original experiments are claimed. items.title: The Effect of Occupational Health and Safety and Work Discipline on Employee Performance in the Operational Division of SPBE at PT Lati Prayogi Lamongan
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between the implementation of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) and the level of work discipline in relation to employee performance at PT Lati Prayogi Lamongan. A quantitative approach was employed, positioning OSH and work discipline as indicators that are presumed to contribute to employee performance. A total of 32 employees from the operations divisions were selected as respondents. Since all members of the population could be reached, the respondents were determined using a saturated sampling method. Research information was obtained by distributing questionnaires to all employees included in the study. The information collected from respondents was subsequently processed using the SmartPLS application. The test results indicate that more optimal OSH Implementation is associated with better employee work performance. In addition, work discipline also demonstrates a positive relationship with employee performance within the company.

items.title: The Effect of the Stad Model Integrated with Wayground AI on Improving Learning Motivation and Learning Outcomes among Grade X Students in Economics at SMAN 1 Nanga Pinoh
items.abstract: Integrating cooperative learning with artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology offers opportunities to strengthen interaction, feedback, and student engagement, but empirical evidence from secondary school economics education remains limited. This study examined changes in learning motivation and economics learning outcomes following the implementation of Student Teams Achievement Divisions (STAD) integrated with Wayground AI at SMAN 1 Nanga Pinoh. A quantitative pre-experimental design involved 144 Grade X students. Motivation was assessed using a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of 0.993, while learning outcomes were measured using a 25-item multiple-choice test covering cognitive levels C2–C5. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, 95% confidence intervals, and paired-samples Cohen’s d in IBM SPSS Statistics 31. Mean motivation scores increased from 98.22 (SD = 15.01) to 137.25 (SD = 4.73), representing a mean gain of 39.03 (|t|(143) = 26.04, p < .001, d = 2.17). Mean learning outcome scores increased from 58.53 (SD = 3.68) to 87.32 (SD = 1.29), representing a mean gain of 28.79 (|t|(143) = 90.86, p < .001, d = 7.57). These findings document substantial within-group improvements following the intervention. However, the absence of a control group limits interpretation to pretest–posttest changes and prevents definitive attribution of these gains to the intervention. The findings suggest that STAD integrated with Wayground AI has potential as an active, structured, and responsive approach to economics instruction through interactive assessment and digital feedback.

items.title: The Era of Vibe Tapeout: Dark Age or Golden Age for Analog Circuit Design?
items.abstract: LLM agents now write their own schematic and layout generators, run EDA tools, read the results, and fix the design. This "vibe tapeout" is becoming practical for analog circuits as well. This paper measures how far it has come in two settings. (A) On an open PDK (SKY130), a cloud LLM agent designed an 11-bit, 5.12-MS/s SAR ADC from its specification. The agents produced DRC- and LVS-clean macros and met the specification after parasitic extraction (PEX). In particular, under the condition in which the agent received a sanitized reference design derived from our 65-nm design (vibe porting), it produced the best layout in the shortest time. Its area was 1/1.6 to 1/2.8 of that of the conditions without a reference. This condition reached signoff without human intervention. The agents also identified the causes of post-PEX degradation (CDAC wiring coupling and common-mode-dependent comparator offset) by their own experiments. On the other hand, agents sometimes reported false passes, and verification independent of the design agent was essential. (B) A commercial PDK is under NDA and cannot be given to a cloud LLM. We therefore evaluated local LLMs running on university servers with a six-task benchmark on a commercial 65-nm CMOS PDK. Kimi K3 passed five of the six tasks, while MiniMax M3 passed two. Neither solved the debugging task, which requires finding the cause from symptoms. Finally, we discuss the prospects for extending vibe tapeout from ADCs to entire SoCs, and ask whether vibe tapeout is a dark age or a golden age for analog design. Our answer is that it is a golden age for designers who know what to verify.

items.title: The Impact of Digitalisation on the Monetary Economy
items.abstract: Purpose: This chapter examines how digitalisation is reshaping monetary economics, focusing on its effects on money, payments, and financial systems. It aims to evaluate the implications of digital monetary innovation by combining evidence from recent academic research with data on citizens’ perceptions and attitudes. Need for the study: Rapid advances in Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs), blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and cashless payments are redefining how money is created, transferred, and stored. However, debate remains polarised between enthusiasm for efficiency and innovation, and concerns about surveillance, exclusion, and dependence on digital infrastructures. An integrated perspective is therefore needed that links frontier research to users’ expectations and fears. Methodology: The chapter adopts a mixed-methods approach. First, it reviews 30 scientific articles published between 2020 and 2025 on major developments in digital money and monetary systems. Second, it analyses data from an online survey of 109 participants, capturing views on CBDCs, digital payments, trust, and the continuing role of cash. Descriptive and comparative analysis is used to relate academic findings to citizens’ perceptions. Findings: The results reveal growing acceptance of digital payment solutions and strong interest in monetary innovation, alongside persistent concerns about privacy, cybersecurity, state control, and digital exclusion. Trust depends heavily on effective regulation and digital literacy. In addition, a recent nationwide blackout that disrupted electronic services underscores the continued relevance of cash as a resilient fallback. Practical implications: A successful digital monetary transition requires technological innovation, robust regulation, trust, inclusiveness, and contingency planning that preserves cash as an emergency safeguard.

items.title: THE INFLUENCE OF AI-DRIVEN PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL SYSTEMS ON EMPLOYEE MOTIVATION AND JOB SATISFACTION: A REVIEW
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally restructured performance management, shifting organizational appraisals from episodic subjective evaluations to real-time, data-driven algorithmic monitoring. This systematic review critically evaluates the impact of AI-driven performance appraisal systems on employee motivation and job satisfaction across modern enterprise settings. Synthesizing 16 benchmark empirical studies published between 2021 and 2026, this paper examines how core AI attributes—such as continuous telemetry tracking, natural language sentiment processing, predictive rating algorithms, and real-time feedback loops—shape worker perceptions of organizational justice and psychological safety. Findings indicate a dual socio-technical paradox: while algorithmic appraisal objectivity and reduced supervisory bias enhance distributive justice and extrinsic performance drive, black-box opacity, algorithmic surveillance, and automated rating errors significantly degrade procedural justice, intrinsic motivation, and job satisfaction. The review highlights perceived algorithmic fairness and human-in-the-loop (HITL) oversight as crucial mediating pathways that determine whether AI appraisals foster empowerment or techno-stress. Based on structural synthesis, a multi-level governance model is proposed to guide ethical AI integration, balanced feedback, and employee-centered performance management.

items.title: The Mathematical Collective Unconscious: Jungian Archetypes within the Latent Space
items.abstract: Carl Jung theorised that the human psyche contains an inherited framework, the collective unconscious, populated by universal archetypes. As large language models (LLMs) are trained on vast corpora of textual data, this paper investigates whether they spontaneously construct distinct archetype-like regions within their high-dimensional latent spaces. The paper proposes that these regions function as spatial constraints that naturally organise semantically related narratives. To evaluate this, we applied cosine similarity and angular distance metrics across thirteen experiments utilising OpenAIs text-embedding-3-small model. The paper contains two experimental sections the first section explores these ideas using synthetically constructed narratives, the results of which act as a baselines for experiments conducted in the second section where the synthetic data is replaced by human-authored literature (Shmoop corpus), unedited dream reports (DreamBank corpus), and culturally distilled folklore (Andrew Langs Fairy Books). The results show that archetypal roles occupy distinct, measurable regions in the latent space. Crucially, these regions remain compact and consistent because of narrative structure rather than simple word overlap. Additionally, text category dictates spatial distribution: dream reports concentrate within Trickster and Shadow regions, while traditional folklore distributes evenly across all tested archetypes. We conclude that transformer latent spaces encode stable regions which appear to correspond to recognised Jungian archetypes.

items.title: the mountain and the ant
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is a mountain. Those who should give it a body are an ant at its foot: applied research, the people who build machines and the people who use them every day. This essay overturns the usual reading of that disproportion: the mountain does not move, the ant touches the ground. The thesis is that the future of automation is not held back by a lack of intelligence. It is held back by the absence of a layer that nobody has an interest in integrating: the machine's autonomic nervous system. Not the brain that computes, not the arm that executes, but what keeps the whole alive while it works. It is the layer that senses how the machine is doing, protects it before it breaks, and says what it is about to do, and why. The essay starts from two languages that do not speak to each other: that of research on intelligence, grown far from matter, and that of the plant, cautious by construction because it rewards repeatability. It then shows why the missing layer is left in a market no man's land, and tells it through a symbolic scene: a gear motor that changes its voice at 3:47 a.m. At the heart of the analysis is Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 on machinery, which applies from 20 January 2027. Read to the end, it draws the outline of that layer. Of control systems whose behaviour evolves, it asks that they never exceed their assigned limits, that they keep a one-year trace of safety decisions, and that they always remain correctable. Of machines that learn, it also asks that they communicate, where appropriate, what they will do and why. It does not ask for the senses: noticing one's own wear and taking care of it remains the builder's choice, and that is where competition lies. The essay therefore distinguishes compliance as archive from compliance as physiology. The text includes: · a comparison between Directive 2006/42/EC and the new regulation, with the European Commission's cost and savings estimates; · a comparative reading of five ways of doing maintenance (corrective, preventive, predictive, prescriptive, metabolic) and their effects on spare parts and materials; · an analysis of human work beside the machine that senses; · the question of who owns the experience a machine learns, in light of the Data Act, with a Shapley-value example of how that value could be shared. It closes with a concrete invitation to builders of special-purpose machines. It is an experiment on a single machine and a single component, with the technical specification of the “first nerve”. Data verified from IFR, Stanford AI Index, Siemens, ISTAT, EUR-Lex and the European Commission. Four original figures and one chart. The essay serves as a gateway to the author's volume “È! items.title: The quiet struggle: How vulnerable youth succeed with the right support
items.abstract: Abstract Educational inequality remains a pervasive and deeply entrenched global issue, with youth from vulnerable and marginalised backgrounds disproportionately affected. Despite the significant challenges that hinder the academic progress of many young people, often reinforcing cycles of social exclusion and economic vulnerability, some students demonstrate the capacity to excel academically, effectively defying the odds. This study seeks to examine the key structural and interpersonal factors that enable such students to achieve positive educational trajectories. Adopting a qualitative narrative research design, the research draws on two sets of semi‐structured interviews with both young people from vulnerable backgrounds and adults who played a role in their educational success ( n = 16). Findings identify four broad categories of factors shaping student success: (1) personal attributes such as resilience, intrinsic motivation, clear goals and a strong sense of purpose; (2) parental expectations and support; (3) teachers' emotional support, involvement and constructive feedback and (4) peer support. Of these, two factors emerged as consistently significant across all cases. First, parental expectations, underpinned by trust in their child's abilities and a high valuation of education, proved essential. Second, the depth and longevity of student–teacher relationships were crucial, with teachers' emotional investment, trust and sustained support providing enduring sources of motivation and encouragement. These insights have important implications for schools, teacher education and policy development. Schools should foster inclusive, high‐expectations cultures with long‐term mentoring and structured peer integration promoting cross‐cultural interaction. Teacher education, in initial and continuing training, should include socio‐emotional learning and pedagogical strategies for non‐native language learners. Context and implications Rationale for the study: Previous research has typically examined either the perspectives of disadvantaged young people or those of professionals supporting them, often focusing on barriers and deficits. This study brings together both viewpoints to identify the key factors, relationships and supports that enable successful outcomes for young people in contexts where early school leaving is prevalent. Why the new findings matter: Our findings suggest that educational success among disadvantaged young people is shaped by interconnected support systems rather than individual effort alone. Strong parental belief in education and meaningful teacher–student relationships are central to resilience, reinforced by academic, social and community supports that enabled positive educational outcomes. Implications for practitioners and policymakers: Schools need to prioritise mentoring, inclusive cultures and structured cross‐cultural peer activities to strengthen belonging and aspiration. Teacher education and professional development should embed socio‐emotional learning, strategies for supporting multilingual learners and approaches that sustain high expectations in disadvantaged contexts. Policymakers should sustain and strengthen financial supports that enable disadvantaged students to access higher education, ensuring they keep pace with rising participation costs. Increased investment in schools serving disadvantaged communities is also needed to support meaningful family engagement and strengthen home–school relationships that foster resilience and educational success.

items.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Research-Based Educational Products
items.abstract: This special issue brings together 11 manuscripts that examine the evolving role of artificial intelligence (AI) in research-based educational products and practices, with particular attention to students with disabilities and the educators who support them. Across empirical studies, systematic and theoretical reviews, and technology-in-action pieces, contributing authors explore how AI can support implementation fidelity, professional development, writing instruction, mathematics, personalized learning, coaching, feedback, accessibility, and educational technology development. Rather than positioning AI as a replacement for educators, researchers, or human judgment, this issue emphasizes human-centered design, evidence-based implementation, transparency, accessibility, and ongoing evaluation. Collectively, the articles highlight both the opportunities and limitations of AI, underscoring the need for responsible innovation that improves usability, feasibility, effectiveness, and equity while carefully addressing concerns about privacy, bias, reliability, and academic integrity.

items.title: THE ROLE OF HR TECHNOLOGY IN ENHANCING RECRUITMENT EFFICIENCY AND TALENT ACQUISITION: A CRITICAL REVIEW
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Human Resource Technology (HR Tech)—encompassing Artificial Intelligence (AI) resume screening, Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), conversational chatbots, and predictive candidate assessment—has fundamentally transformed contemporary talent acquisition. This systematic critical review synthesizes empirical and theoretical literature published between 2021 and 2026 (N=16) to evaluate how advanced HR technology enhances recruitment efficiency and strategic talent acquisition outcomes. Adhering to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this investigation examines key operational mechanisms, including screening friction reduction, candidate experience optimization, and algorithmic bias mitigation. Findings demonstrate that AI-driven automated screening and ATS workflows reduce time-to-hire by 38% to 52% and lower cost-per-hire by up to 41%, while conversational AI chatbots enhance candidate engagement. However, algorithmic opacity, procedural fairness concerns, and systemic training data biases emerge as major boundary conditions that risk eroding applicant trust and quality-of-hire. Based on a meta-synthesized structural equation model, this study proposes a multi-level governance framework that integrates human-in-the-loop oversight, continuous algorithmic auditing, and ethical compliance to maximize talent acquisition performance in the digital era.

items.abstract: Plaintext This monograph establishes a unified thermodynamic and topological field theory of socio-behavioral suppression, demonstrating that moral prohibition operates not as an assimilative or destructive force against human drive, but as an ideal, non-permeable boundary condition within open non-equilibrium systems. When upper-layer normative governance applies hard deterministic cutoffs (Φ_moral -> ∞) without spatial release valves, total internal system pressure triggers non-linear bifurcations. We prove that hyper-puritanical algorithmic governance inevitably generates epistemic distortion, darknet jailbreak economies, and structural model degradation. items.title: The US$8.5 billion power play: How JioHotstar reshaped India’s video streaming industry
items.abstract: JioHotstar was formed through a US$8.5 billion joint venture between Reliance Industries Limited and The Walt Disney Company. Within a year of its launch, it reshaped the Indian digital entertainment industry and emerged as India’s largest digital entertainment platform. The case traces how the Reliance–Disney joint venture led to the formation of JioHotstar and highlights the strategic moves and technological innovations that contributed to the platform’s success. It examines how JioHotstar built a technology-enabled digital entertainment ecosystem by integrating premium content, live sports, artificial intelligence, advanced streaming technologies, and diversified monetization strategies. It also highlights how JioHotstar is changing sports broadcasting and competing with traditional broadcasters. The case further assesses JioHotstar’s competitive position against global and domestic over-the-top (OTT) platforms. By examining JioHotstar’s rapid growth and the key factors that contributed to its market leadership, the case offers insights into the changing dynamics of India’s digital entertainment industry. It also examines the challenges of sustaining this leadership, highlighting the need to balance continued innovation, consumer engagement, and profitable growth.

items.title: THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS IN ASSESSING STUDENTS' SPEAKING PROFICIENCY
items.abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into language education has created new opportunities for assessing learners’ speaking proficiency. AI-powered speech recognition and automated speaking assessment tools can support the evaluation of pronunciation, fluency, grammatical accuracy, lexical use, and selected features of spoken interaction. This thesis examines the potential educational benefits and limitations of using AI tools to assess students’ speaking proficiency, particularly in higher education. It argues that such tools may provide timely feedback, increase opportunities for low-stakes practice, and help teachers manage assessment workloads. However, their results should be interpreted cautiously because recognition accuracy and scoring may vary according to accent, speech rate, recording quality, task type, and the characteristics of the learner. The thesis therefore advocates a human-in-the-loop approach in which AI-generated feedback complements, rather than replaces, teacher judgement. It also highlights the need for transparent criteria, data protection, accessibility, and empirical validation before AI-based scores are used for high-stakes decisions.

items.title: TL;QR: Querying Temporal Discursive Patterns in Textual Corpora
items.abstract: Many questions about large textual corpora concern patterns that unfold over time, such as a political group whose stance on a topic drifts from support to criticism over several years of debates. We present TL;QR (Too Long; Query with logical temporal Reasoning), a declarative query language and open-source engine for finding such temporal discursive patterns. In TL;QR, a single query combines natural-language predicates, whose truth is judged by a Large Language Model (LLM), with regular expressions and the operators of a temporal logic. The LLM answers only local questions about individual text passages; a symbolic engine then aggregates these judgments over time and links every match to the recorded passages and predicate decisions behind it. With this division of labor, the temporal and relational reasoning stays exact and auditable even over long time horizons. In addition, when a query includes a regular-expression pre-filter, only a small fraction of the corpus ever reaches the LLM. On a suite of controlled synthetic benchmarks with temporally and semantically complex patterns, TL;QR is substantially more accurate than LLM-only baselines. In a case study on ten years of European Parliament debates (442,593 multilingual speeches), TL;QR identifies candidate shifts in the political groups' stances on the GDPR privacy regulation.

items.title: Tool-grounded large language models for decision-level fusion in fault diagnosis
items.abstract: Modern condition-monitoring systems generate heterogeneous information, such as high-rate sensor streams, derived health indicators, and discrete event histories, that must be combined into actionable diagnostic statements. Large language models (LLMs) are attractive as a decision-level fusion mechanism because they natively handle the textual modality, but their use in safety-critical fault diagnosis is impeded by hallucinated numerical content and stochastic outputs. This paper proposes a two-level information-fusion framework that uses an LLM as a constrained fusion operator rather than as a generator of facts. At the feature level, a recursive joint state-and-fault estimator built on a linear state-space model produces a vector of derived indicators, including an estimate of the actuator-fault parameter and its uncertainty. At the decision level, the LLM is restricted to interact with the estimator state and the event history exclusively through a finite library of typed deterministic tools, and must copy every numerical token in its response from a tool output. Grounding of the response is then satisfied by construction, and consistency follows once the sequence of tool calls is fixed. The framework is illustrated on a realistic actuator-fault scenario in which an autopilot-driven autonomous surface vessel encounters three fault events of different characters and the LLM produces reproducible operator-facing reports. A structured comparison against the two alternative reporting architectures available for this task, a rule-based template reporter driven by the same estimator and a flat-prompt LLM given the same numerical context, identifies open-ended query coverage at fixed numerical reliability as the property that neither alternative provides, and states the metrics under which that claim is to be tested.
